title: The diagonal detects extension of the group difference map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme smooth over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and $G$ a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme with identity $e$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open and $f:U\to G$ a $k$-morphism. Write $\Delta:X\to X\times_kX$ for the diagonal [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $\Omega\subseteq X\times_kX$ be any open subscheme containing $\Delta(X)$. Put $H=\Omega\cap(U\times_kU)$ and let $\phi:H\to G$ be the morphism $\phi(x,y)=f(x)f(y)^{-1}$, formed from the multiplication and inverse of $G$. Define
$$D=\bigcup\{V\subseteq X\text{ open}:\ \exists F_V:V\to G\text{ over }k,\ F_V|_{V\cap U}=f|_{V\cap U}\},$$
$$B=\bigcup\{N\subseteq\Omega\text{ open}:\ \exists b_N:N\to G\text{ over }k,\ b_N|_{N\cap H}=\phi|_{N\cap H}\}.$$
There is a unique $k$-morphism $b:B\to G$ restricting to every $b_N$, and
$$\Delta^{-1}(B)=D,\qquad b\circ\Delta|_D=e\circ(D\to\operatorname{Spec}k).$$
These are assertions about scheme morphisms and all scheme points; no $k$-rational point of $U$ and no geometric integrality of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, printed p.17, first paragraph of the proof: difference map and its diagonal extension criterion; scheme-theoretic formulation over arbitrary k, with the descent argument detailed in the report.

proof.text: First record the density needed below. The field spectrum is Noetherian (its affine coordinate ring has only the ideals $0,k$), so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus $U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact: the ascending-chain condition on opens forces every open covering of an open to have a finite subcover. Since $X$ is integral, it is reduced; [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic], applied to this dense open immersion, says its scheme-theoretic image is $X$. Here an open immersion is quasi-separated since its diagonal is an isomorphism. Consequently $U$ is schematically dense. We will use density on open restrictions and its transitivity: on each open these assert respectively restriction of an injective section map and composition of two injective section maps. These observations also identify the image formulation with $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ injective.

The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, hence so is $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]; both are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The second projection $X\times_kX\to X$ and the first projection $X\times_kU\to X$ are their base changes along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] first to $U\hookrightarrow X$ and the second projection $X\times_kX\to X$ to obtain the dense open $X\times_kU$. Apply it again to $U\hookrightarrow X$ and the first projection $X\times_kU\to X$. Transitivity from step 1 gives schematic density of $U\times_kU$ in $X\times_kX$. Restriction to any open $N\subseteq\Omega$ gives schematic density of $N\cap H$ in $N$. The quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness assumptions in the density lemma concern the original open immersion $U\hookrightarrow X$, verified in step 1. Also $G$ is separated as an absolute scheme: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated since its diagonal is given by the surjective multiplication map $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k\to k$, and composition of separated morphisms is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Thus even the absolute separated-target version of the equality lemma below applies.

Two extensions $b_N,b_{N'}$ agree on $N\cap N'\cap H$, schematically dense in $N\cap N'$ by step 2. Hence they agree on the whole overlap by [lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open]. The separated-target hypothesis is verified in step 2. Gluing the underlying continuous maps and, on each target open, the compatible homomorphisms of structure sheaves produces a morphism $b:B\to G$; its local-ring property and its being over $k$ hold on the covering by the $N$. Uniqueness holds on that same covering. In particular $b|_H=\phi$, since $H$ itself is one of the extension opens.

source.place: Tag 01RH (lemma-equality-of-morphisms); gluing of morphisms on an open covering by the sheaf axiom

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq X$ admit an extension $F_V$. On $N=\Omega\cap(V\times_kV)$ the group operations [def-sc-group-scheme] define $c= m(F_Vp_1,\operatorname{inv}(F_Vp_2))$. On $N\cap H$ this is $\phi$, so $N\subseteq B$. Since $\Omega$ contains the diagonal, $\Delta^{-1}(N)=V$. Taking the union over all such $V$ gives $D\subseteq\Delta^{-1}(B)$. Moreover $c\Delta|_V=e$ by the group inverse identity, as an identity of morphisms, valid on every test scheme.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, printed p.17, forward diagonal implication

proof.text: For the converse take any scheme point $x$ with $\Delta(x)\in B$. Choose an extension open $N\subseteq\Omega$ containing $\Delta(x)$, with extension $c:N\to G$. Put $T=N\cap(X\times_kU)$, and $q=p_1|_T:T\to X$. The fibre $N_x$ is a nonempty open of $X_{\kappa(x)}$: it contains the point supplied by the diagonal. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat: its unique local-ring map is the field extension, whose tensor functor is exact by [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact]. Its base change $X_{\kappa(x)}\to X$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Thus [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] makes $U_{\kappa(x)}$ schematically, hence topologically, dense in $X_{\kappa(x)}$. It meets $N_x$, proving $T_x\ne\varnothing$ and $x\in q(T)$. The projection $X\times_kU\to X$ is the base change of the flat, locally finitely presented $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (step 2), so it is flat and, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], an open map. Its restriction $q$ to the open $T$ has the same local rings and maps opens of $T$ to opens; thus $q$ is flat and open, and $W=q(T)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$.

source.place: Tag 081H (lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open), 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image); Milne I Lemma 3.3, p.17, converse, replacing a chosen rational point by the whole covering T

proof.text: View $q:T\to W$ as a surjection; it is flat, its local rings being those of step 5. It is a singleton fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for an affine open $W_0\subseteq W$, affine opens of $q^{-1}W_0$ have open images covering $W_0$, since $q$ is open by step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]; quasi-compactness of $W_0$ gives finitely many such images. Define $a:T\to G$ by $a=m(c,f p_2)$ using [def-sc-group-scheme]. On $q^{-1}(W\cap U)=N\cap(U\times_kU)$ the identity $(f(x)f(y)^{-1})f(y)=f(x)$ gives $a=fq$. This is an identity of morphisms by associativity and inverse in the group object, without a commutativity assumption.

source.place: Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering); Milne I Lemma 3.3, p.17, formula f(x)=Phi(x,u) f(u)

proof.text: Put $R=T\times_WT$ with projections $r_1,r_2$. The projection $r_1$ is the base change of the flat $q$ along $q$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], so $R\to W$, which is $q r_1$, is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose]. The open $W\cap U$ is schematically dense in $W$ by step 1; its immersion is quasi-compact because $W\subseteq X$ is Noetherian. Therefore [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] makes its inverse image schematically dense in $R$. On this inverse image, step 6 gives $ar_1=fqr_1=fqr_2=ar_2$. By the separated-target equality principle [lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open], $ar_1=ar_2$ on $R$. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] with base $W$, covering $T\to W$, source the identity $W$-scheme, and target $G\times_kW$. Its compatibility equation is precisely this equality, so it produces $F_W:W\to G$ over $k$ with $F_Wq=a$. On $W\cap U$ it equals $f$: the uniqueness clause of the same descent lemma, applied to the restricted covering, identifies them after the equality in step 6. Thus $x\in W\subseteq D$. This proves $\Delta^{-1}(B)\subseteq D$ for all scheme points.

Steps 4 and 7 prove equality of the two open subschemes $\Delta^{-1}(B)=D$. For each extension open $V$ in the definition of $D$, the map $c$ constructed in step 4 agrees with $b$ on $\Omega\cap(V\times_kV)$ by step 3. Pulling back along $\Delta|_V$ and using step 4 gives $b\Delta|_V=e$. These opens cover $D$, so the morphism equality holds on $D$. All constructions used scheme morphisms and residue fields; none required $U(k)\ne\varnothing$, or integrality of any product or field extension of $X$.

This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Supporting input in the level-rigidity proof: Chapter I, Theorem 10.15, printed p.49 (finite free Hom conclusion); §10 endomorphism-ring convention, printed pp.42–43. Auxiliary for this split: An abelian inclusion retracts up to a positive integer. Supporting input: 8.18, printed p.152 (combine 8.16 and 8.17). Uniqueness is the separated-target equality principle on an integral source. This is the extension theorem, not extension to an arbitrary proper target. Sublemma: Milne 8.17, divisorial indeterminacy for a smooth source and a group target, combined with 8.16 in 8.18. Auxiliary: The diagonal detects extension of the group difference map.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-eb830dd78 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX for one citation fault (C4); full review in review.md. There are no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Source checked: Milne AV I Lemma 3.3, printed pp.17-18. The difference map Φ(x,y)=φ(x)φ(y)^{-1} and the rule Φ(x,x)=e match step 4. Milne's converse picks a point u and sets φ(x)=Φ(x,u)φ(u); the delivery replaces this with fpqc descent of a=c·f(p2) along q:T→W, and that replacement is a faithful scheme-theoretic version. I read all 8 steps against each cited statement. Density: U is schematically dense because X is integral and Noetherian, then flat pullbacks give density of U×U in X×X, of U_κ(x) in X_κ(x) and in R. Equality on R uses the absolutely separated G (Spec k→Spec Z is separated, plus proper-fp-permanence (e)). The fpqc condition holds through open images of affine opens, so q need not be quasi-compact. The cocycle condition of lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend reduces exactly to a r1=a r2, and its uniqueness on W∩U gives F_W=f there. The group identity a=f q needs no commutativity. Edge cases tested: U=X, constant f, X=Spec L with L/k finite separable and X×X disconnected, non-closed x. Fault: steps 2, 5 and 7 took scheme smoothness, flatness and base change from the stack node lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus, which does not state that its chart-tested properties agree with the scheme properties. Repaired with the Mathlib leaves lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition, lem-pc-smooth-flat, lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change and lem-pc-flat-compose, plus the base-change clause of lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open for openness of q. Steps 2 and 5-7 are rewritten and uses/proof_deps rebuilt in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-group-difference-diagonal-domain.json. Batch-5 finding: the stack node reaches only def-trf-algebraic-space, a general definition and not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so it would not force a RETURN; after the FIX the item no longer cites it. Tool use lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend accepted as generic descent of morphisms. No SGA cited.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
